newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish yields ended lower on the back of stronger European and U.S. markets. The crown weakened some against the mark in very quiet trade but was stronger against a generally weaker dollar.
A statement by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan sent European and U.S. yields falling since dealers interpreted it as diminished possibilities of a rate hike in May.
"The trade in crowns was very thin. Some importing companies bought dollars against crowns," one dealer said.
The downward movement in yields was helped by lower foreign yields since domestic news was sparse due to a Swedish holiday.

"There has not been any domestic news to trade on so we have followed foreign yields. The yields in high yielding countries fell more than in other countries and Sweden was a part of that movement," one dealer said.
The market is focussing on further developments on Sweden's position towards the European economic and monetary union as well as the release of Sweden's April inflation data on May 15.

Six month T-bill rates dropped two basis points to 4.20 percent and ten year bond yield fell eight basis points to 7.03 percent. The crown softened to 4.5330 against the mark versus 4.5000 crowns on Wednesday. On Thursday markets were closed.
